Returns the visitor traffic over a period of time.

The traffic metrics are reported in five-minute intervals:
- Total number of human visitors
- Total number of good bot visitors
- Total number of bad bot visitors
- Total number of unknown bot visitors

_Human visitors_ are non-bot visitors. _Good bots_ are a list of well-known bots, including Googlebot, Bingbot, and so on).
_Bad bots_ are a list of known bad bots, including Grinchbots, AhrefsBot, and so on. _Unknown bots_ are visitors that are likely 
bots but are not in the good or bad bot lists.

description.content: Allows you to retrieve waiting room telemetry per waiting room, per minute. Gets metrics for a specific waiting room. Optionally provide _start_ and _end_ filter for a specific period. Ninety days of metrics are kept.

query.description: The start date and time used for querying metrics data. Must be provided in RFC3339 date-time format and be in UTC.
The end date and time used for querying metrics data. Must be provided in RFC3339 date-time format and be in UTC.

Represents the starting point from where to begin fetching the metrics records. This parameter is especially useful in conjunction with the _limit_ parameter for pagination of a large number of metrics records. By default, it is set to 0, meaning that data retrieval will start from the very first record. For example, if you have 10,000 metrics records and set the _limit_ to 100, then the first API call without an offset will retrieve records 1 to 100. If you set the _offset_ to 100 for the next call, you will retrieve records 101 to 200, and so on. This way, by incrementing the _offset_ by the _limit_ value for successive calls, you can paginate through the entire dataset.
The _limit_ parameter determines the number of metrics returned.
The field used for sorting.

The sort order:
 * _asc_ - Ascending, from A to Z
 * _desc_ - Descending, from Z to A
